chapter_title: Concerning Four Hunters of Light and Four of Darkness
chapter_note: The substrate is a well-preserved four-fold parallel enumeration mapping cosmic agents to hunter correspondences (net, ship, sea). Both light and dark series follow the same structural template. The substrate is dominant in the light hunters (except P4 where 'his holy church' intrudes) and in the first three dark hunters. The fourth dark hunter (P11) is almost entirely overwritten by editorial bridge material identifying 'every sect' and 'erroneous teaching' in the contemporary world. Two exhortation beatitudes close each series. The substrate vocabulary drops sharply in the second half, consistent with editorial fatigue replacing the fourth dark hunter's cosmic content with polemical application.

paragraphs.core_text: There are four hunters who were sent from the light to fulfill the will of the greatness.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Once again the apostle speaks to his disciples:' — dialogue frame attribution formula.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Standard frame formula wrapping a substantive cosmological statement that defines the four-fold teaching structure. The statement itself is substrate: it declares the enumeration and its cosmic origin.

paragraphs.core_text: The first hunter is the First Man who was sent from the greatness. He threw himself down to the five storehouses of Darkness, he caught and siezed the enmity [... ...] his net also [... ...] out over all the children of Darkness [... ...]. His ship is his four sons who are swathed over his body. The sea is the land of Darkness [... ...]; his net is [...] and his powers.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure cosmic-to-cosmic mapping. Net, ship, sea all map to cosmic entities/domains: net = powers, ship = four sons (cosmic emanations), sea = land of Darkness. 'Five storehouses of Darkness' is signature substrate vocabulary. Both sides of every correspondence stay within the cosmic system. Heavily lacunose but structure intact.

paragraphs.core_text: The second hunter is the Third Ambassador. This one, for by his light image, which he revealed to the depths below, he hunted after the entire light that is in all things; as it is established in them. His net is his light image, [...] the whole universe and took it prisoner, to this likeness [... His] ship is his light ship. [The sea] is the universe [...] which were hunted after by his net [...] his [glorious] image.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure substrate. The Third Ambassador is a cosmic emanation. Net = light image (cosmic manifestation), ship = light ship (cosmic vehicle), sea = universe (cosmic domain). All mappings cosmos→cosmos. Despite lacunae, the correspondential structure is fully preserved.

paragraphs.core_text: The third hunter is Jesus the Splendour, who came from the greatness, who hunts after the light and life; and he [...] it to the heights. His net is his wisdom, [the] light wisdom with which he hunts the souls, catching them in the net. The sea is the error of the universe, the souls that are drowning in it [...]. He catches them in his net. They are the souls [... th]em by his light wisdom.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'His ship is his holy church [...].' — institutional layer; maps the cosmic 'ship' correspondence to the Manichaean church, breaking the cosmos→cosmos pattern (cf. ship = four sons in P2, ship = light ship in P3, ship = light cloud in P5). Also removed 'the law of sin [...],' — editorial bridge vocabulary echoing Pauline language (Romans 8:2), inserted between substrate identifications of the sea.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Jesus the Splendour (Isho Ziwa) is a cosmic entity in the emanation hierarchy, not the historical Jesus. The substrate third hunter is preserved with net = wisdom (cosmic attribute) and sea = error of the universe (cosmic condition). The editorial hand inserted 'his holy church' for the ship and 'the law of sin' as a gloss, both mapping one side outside the cosmic system. Gardner's synopsis confirms: 'Jesus, whose net is the wisdom cast from the church' — the church connection is editorial.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth hunter is the great counsel that [...] that lives in the circuit [...] ⟨p.29⟩ entire universe in it today. Yet, at the end, in the dissolution of the universe, this very counsel of life will gather itself in and sculpt its soul in the Last Statue. Its net is its Living Spirit, because with its Spirit it can hunt after the light and the life that is in all things; and build it upon its body. Its ship, in which it is established, is this light cloud whereby it itself travels in the five elements [...], the great fire that will burn all the buildings of [... ...] in its net is the light and the life. It can rescue and free it from all bonds and fetters.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Richest substrate paragraph. Net = Living Spirit (cosmic entity), ship = light cloud traveling in the five elements (cosmic vehicle in cosmic domain), the dissolution and Last Statue = cosmic eschatology. 'Today' describes the cosmic phase (the counsel currently lives in the circuit), not the editor's present — both sides stay within cosmic temporality. 'Five elements,' 'Last Statue,' 'bonds and fetters,' 'dissolution of the universe' — all systematic cosmic process vocabulary. The 'great counsel' / 'counsel of life' is a cosmic entity, mirrored by the 'evil counsel' in P9.

Beatitude closure appended to the light-hunter teaching sequence. 'Blessed is every one who...' is the signature exhortation formula. The seam flag correctly identifies this as a devotional wrapper. The reference to 'the great fire' picks up cosmic vocabulary from P5 but pivots to moral application and audience address.

Editorial transition paragraph. 'Once again he speaks' is dialogue frame formula. 'As I have revealed to you... I will also teach you' is self-referential editorial voice — the compiler narrating his own teaching act. The cosmological terms ('four living hunters of light,' 'four evil hunters who came from the darkness') summarize/preview but are entirely embedded in first-person editorial self-reference. The teaching structure does not require this transition; the enumeration in P8 introduces the dark hunters directly.

paragraphs.core_text: The first hunter is the King of they who belong to the Darkness, who hunted after the living soul with his net at the beginning of the worlds. His net is his fire and his lust that he has put upon the living soul, with which he has entangled it [...], through all his powers.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure substrate. The King of Darkness mapped as hunter: net = fire and lust (cosmic attributes of the dark realm). 'At the beginning of the worlds' is cosmic temporal frame. 'The living soul' is the cosmic entity being hunted. All mappings cosmos→cosmos. Mirrors the structure of the light hunters exactly.

paragraphs.core_text: [The] second hunter is the evil counsel that lives in [...] that hunts after the light [...] and [...] up from [...] the earths to heaven. It binds them with its powers, which bring them to the heavenly worlds above. Its net is [...] whereby they are drawn up from the abyss [to the heig]hts.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Substrate despite heavy lacunae. The 'evil counsel' mirrors the 'great counsel' (P5) — systematic cosmic parallelism. Cosmic geography: earths, heaven, abyss, heights. The 'evil counsel' that draws light upward from the abyss to the heavenly worlds is a cosmic counter-agent. All mappings stay within the cosmic system. The binding and drawing-up describe cosmic processes, not contemporary institutions.

paragraphs.core_text: The third hunter is lust [...] walks in every power of the flesh that walks [...] in the [...] the living souls [... ...] them in its bodies, which [... ...].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Very fragmentary but the preserved vocabulary is all cosmic: lust as a cosmic force (not moral exhortation), 'every power of the flesh' (cosmic powers embodied in matter), 'the living souls' (cosmic entities), 'its bodies' (the material forms that imprison souls). Despite lacunae, the cosmos→cosmos pattern is discernible.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth [hunter is the spirit] of Darkness.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed all content after the cosmic identification. 'The law of sin and death' — Pauline editorial vocabulary (cf. Romans 8:2). 'That rules in every sect' — maps cosmic spirit to the editor's contemporary religious landscape ('every sect' is POINTING AT). 'Erroneous teaching full of guile and villainy and wicked turns' — editorial characterization of contemporary false religions. 'Eternal punishment' (×2) — eschatological warning. 'Foolish people' — editorial address. 'Its net... is its erroneous teaching' — the net correspondence maps to 'erroneous teaching,' which is a contemporary phenomenon, not a cosmic domain (contrast: net = fire and lust in P8, net = Living Spirit in P5). The entire description after the cosmic identity has been overwritten by editorial bridge material identifying the dark spirit's activity in contemporary sects.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The substrate REQUIRES a fourth dark hunter (the enumeration demands it), and 'the spirit of Darkness' is the cosmic entity filling that position. But the substrate description — which should have included cosmic correspondences for net, ship, and sea parallel to the other hunters — has been almost entirely replaced by editorial bridge material. The editorial_bridge score (12.66) is the highest in the chapter. The editor uses the fourth hunter position to polemicize against competing religious movements ('every sect,' 'erroneous teaching'). This is the clearest example in the chapter of one side of the mapping reaching into the contemporary world.

Beatitude closure for the dark-hunter sequence, parallel to P6. 'Blessed is every one who...' formula. 'Knowledge' (gnosis) as the means of escape and 'bond and fetter for ever and ever' as devotional closure. The seam flag correctly identifies this as editorial appendage to the teaching sequence.
